title: Overflip: Repetition-Induced Label Flips in Guardrail Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.15013v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Guardrail models are classifiers deployed to screen malicious prompts and responses in LLM-based services. To meet latency constraints, many lightweight guardrails adopt compact Transformer backbones (e.g., DeBERTa) that are trained with short context windows (typically 512 tokens) and rely on bucketed relative positional encodings to process longer inputs. Prior evaluations assume that a guardrail's decision is stable as the input is lengthened. We show that this assumption can fail. We identify Overflip, a repetition-induced instability where repeating a prompt causes the guardrail's prediction to flip (MAL$\to$BEN) as the sequence grows. We conduct experiments on 9 widely used lightweight guardrail models. Five exhibit MAL$\to$BEN flips on a benchmark of 100 prompts, with confidence margins shrinking steadily with repetition. Among these vulnerable models, flip rates range from 8% to 92%, with first flips occurring at roughly 2.6k--9.

translated_title: Overflip：护栏模型中由重复引发的标签翻转
translated_abstract: 护栏模型是部署在基于LLM的服务中用于筛查恶意提示和响应的分类器。为了满足延迟约束，许多轻量级护栏采用紧凑的Transformer骨干网络（例如DeBERTa），这些模型使用较短的上下文窗口（通常为512个token）进行训练，并依赖分桶相对位置编码来处理更长的输入。先前的评估假设护栏的决策在输入变长时会保持稳定。我们证明这一假设可能失效。我们识别出一种名为Overflip的由重复引发的不稳定性：重复一个提示会导致护栏的预测随序列增长而发生翻转（MAL→BEN，即从恶意变为良性）。我们在9个广泛使用的轻量级护栏模型上进行了实验，其中五个模型在包含100个提示的基准测试中表现出MAL→BEN翻转，且其置信度边际随重复次数稳步缩小。在这些易受攻击的模型中，翻转率介于8%到92%之间，首次翻转大约发生在2.6k到9.x token处（摘要内容在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文发现了"Overflip"现象：轻量级LLM护栏模型在提示被重复而输入变长时，其分类预测会从恶意翻转为良性，暴露出此类模型处理长输入时的严重不稳定性。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies "Overflip," a repetition-induced instability where lightweight LLM guardrail models flip their predictions from malicious to benign as prompts are repeated and inputs grow longer.
